findings.title: next_month does not roll over the year at December
findings.description: next_month() computes the new month as int(m) + 1 without checking for overflow past 12. For an input like "2026-12" this returns "2026-13", an invalid month key. rollover_budgets() (and any other caller) will silently write budgets with month="2026-13", which will never match any real month in queries like budget_status() or future rollover_budgets() calls, causing December-to-January rollovers to be lost silently.

findings.title: rollover_budgets silently overwrites an existing budget for the target month
findings.description: set_budget() is an upsert (per test_budget_upsert). If the user has already set a budget for the target month (e.g. they set next month's budget in advance, or ran rollover twice), rollover_budgets() will overwrite it with from_month's limit + carry, discarding the previously configured limit without warning. This is a silent data-loss bug for a feature explicitly meant to run at month end, when overlap with pre-existing next-month budgets is plausible.

findings.title: test_rollover asserts nothing meaningful
findings.description: The final assertion `assert len(status) >= 0` is always true regardless of behavior (list length is never negative), so the test cannot fail even if rollover_budgets is completely broken. It never checks the returned target month value, the new budget's limit_cents/rolled-over amount, or the December year-boundary case, so it would not catch the next_month() overflow bug or the overwrite-existing-budget bug described above.
